Released at 2026-10-22

* SECURITY: **The base images of the release Dockerfiles are pinned by digest (the shipped image contents are unchanged; no change to image versions or runtime behaviour).** `Dockerfile.logs`, `Dockerfile.traces` and `Dockerfile.datagen` now read `image:tag@sha256:<digest>` on every `FROM` line, for the distroless runtime base and for the Go builder image (the digest of the multi-arch index, so linux/amd64 and linux/arm64 both resolve), and keep their human-readable tags. The Go image of the parity compose file is pinned the same way, and the temporary entries for these files are removed from `scripts/ci/image_pins_allowlist.txt`.
* SECURITY: **The parity ratchet holds one pass floor per signal, and a skipped parity test now fails the run (CI and test tooling only; no change to the Lakehouse binaries or to runtime behaviour).** `scripts/ci/parity_ratchet.py` read one combined `min-pass` floor, so a whole signal's unlocked results (all logs results, or all traces results) could skip or disappear while the job stayed green. `tests/parity/known_failures.txt` now also holds `min-pass-logs` and `min-pass-traces`, set to the lowest pass count of the last five green runs on `main` (669 logs results, 418 traces results, 1192 in total), and the ratchet fails when a signal falls below its floor or reports no result at all; a result belongs to a signal by the name rules of `signal_of`, and a unit test fails for any `tests/parity` test that no rule names. A test that reports `skip` fails the run unless the allowlist lists it as `# expected-skip: <test>  # <reason>`; an entry whose test stops skipping is stale. The registry gate holds the new floors as it holds `min-pass` (they only go up) and fails a PR that adds an expected skip. The 19 places in the traces parity tests that skipped when the hot or the cold tier returned nothing (14 in `coldhot_endpoint_parity_test.go`, 4 in `traces_parity_test.go`, 1 in `servicegraph_parity_test.go`) now wait up to 30 seconds for the data and then fail with the evidence; no assertion was weakened. The parity summary and the PR quality report print logs and traces results side by side.
* SECURITY: **The registry gate recognises digest pins on the base images of the release Dockerfiles (CI only; no change to the Lakehouse binaries or to runtime behaviour).** `scripts/ci/pr_classify.py` and its Go twin in `tests/conformance/registry` now accept an optional `@sha256:` digest (exactly 64 lowercase hex characters) after the tag of the Go builder image, so a toolchain bump can move the tag and the digest together and a build container in the parity stack can be pinned. A change to the `FROM` lines of `Dockerfile`, `Dockerfile.logs` or `Dockerfile.traces` that only adds, removes or changes the digest of an image, with the image name, tag, platform and stage name equal, is no longer classed as a product change. Everything else in those files, a digest without a tag and any malformed digest still are. The shared fixture gains the accepted and rejected cases for both twins.
* SECURITY: **The external-reader test matrix uses a patched release of a transitive Python dependency (test tooling only; no change to the Lakehouse binaries or to runtime behaviour).** `thrift` moves from 0.16.0 to 0.24.0 in `tests/readers/requirements.txt`, which closes Dependabot alerts 29, 30 and 31. `parquet-tools` pins `thrift` below 0.17, so it is now installed from its own hashed file, `tests/readers/requirements-parquet-tools.txt`, after the main lock and without dependency resolution; its other dependencies are listed in `requirements.in`. Only the `readers-inprocess` job installs it.
* SECURITY: **The vulnerability scan can now fail the build, and the release images are scanned (CI only; no change to the Lakehouse binaries or to runtime behaviour).** The required `trivy` check scans the repository for fixable HIGH and CRITICAL vulnerabilities (and for secrets) and exits non-zero on a finding; before, it could only report. The vulnerability database is downloaded in a step of its own (`scripts/ci/trivy_fetch_db.sh`: three mirrors, three rounds, the cached copy as a last resort), so a registry or network problem is reported as such and is never mistaken for a finding. New `trivy-image-logs`, `trivy-image-logs-fips`, `trivy-image-traces` and `trivy-image-traces-fips` jobs build the release images from the repository Dockerfiles with the release build arguments (nothing is pushed) and apply the same policy to each, and `trivy-gate-fixture` shows on every run that the scan fails on a fixture with a known fixable vulnerability and passes on a clean one. Exceptions go in a reviewed `.trivyignore`, one reason and one expiry date per entry. `scripts/ci/tests/test_trivy_gate.py` fails if a trivy step loses its exit code, severity or fixed-only policy, if a scan runs without the separate database step, or if a release image is no longer scanned.

* BUGFIX: **Only `FIPS=1` builds an image with the FIPS 140 module: the default images were built with it too ([#685](https://github.com/ReliablyObserve/victoria-lakehouse/issues/685)).** `Dockerfile.logs` and `Dockerfile.traces` set `ENV GOFIPS140=${FIPS:+v1.0.0}` after `ARG FIPS=0`, and in `${VAR:+word}` a variable set to `0` still counts as set, so the default `lakehouse-logs` and `lakehouse-traces` images and the `-fips` images were the same binary (`GOFIPS140=v1.0.0-c2097c7c`, `-tags=fips140v1.0`, `DefaultGODEBUG=fips140=on`). Both Dockerfiles now export `GOFIPS140=v1.0.0` in the build step only when `FIPS` equals `1`, so the default images use Go's standard crypto and `fips-status` reports `disabled`, as documented; the `-fips` images are built with the same settings as before (the new `-fips` `lakehouse-logs` binary is byte-identical to the one the old default build produced). The default images change as a result: their crypto is the standard library instead of the FIPS 140-3 module (the binary is 0.3-0.5 % larger, measured on linux/arm64; `fips140=on` is no longer the built-in default), and operators who relied on the default image being FIPS must switch to the `-fips` tag. `scripts/ci/tests/test_fips_build_arg.py` fails if a Dockerfile selects the module with anything other than an exact `"$FIPS" = "1"` comparison, and the `trivy-image` jobs now run `scripts/ci/check_fips_variant.sh` (`go version -m`) and `fips-status` on the image built for each of the four release variants.
